title: The kitty, and Nick Gagliano's family anniversary party
summary: Bands kept kitties for tips. He describes attorney Nick Gagliano, manager of the George Lewis band, and the Gagliano relatives in medical school.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, most places had a cigar box or a milk bottle or a can, I think quite frequently supplied by the band, sometimes marked kitty, sometimes just discreetly displayed on top of the piano or in front, and sometimes with a sign saying feed the kitty. And people tended to fairly regularly. I remember one particularly enjoyable occasion, which I think I got invited to kind of late and wound up, I believe, only Greenwood and I went. But the manager of the George Lewis band at the time was a fellow, an attorney named Nick Gagliano. Nick, I had met following bands around, and I think also at the New Orleans Jazz Club meetings, and he was a nice kind of a guy. And when I went to medical school, which I started a little after I met Nick, this was in fall, I started in fall of 48, I found out that one of my classmates was also named Nick Gagliano, and this was a cousin of the attorney, and one of the faculty people, the ancillary faculty, was also Gagliano, and I think he was Nick too. And they were all related. And somewhere along the line, I think probably in 49 or 50, conceivably 51, one of the Knicks, and I think the attorneys, parents had their 25th wedding anniversary, and they rented, this was on a Sunday, they rented a large club in Jefferson Parish off the airline highway, and invited all the family, and they also invited me, and I think Greenwood.
